Bundled OpenSSL excludes the separately noticed SipHash implementation through no-siphash and no-quic; old and failed single-option binaries are rejected by the exclusion gate. Current static core 66e7213d passed 35 container and 29 HTTPS checks. It still contains non-allowlisted Rust Unicode data, while libc, unwind, compiler-builtins and startup inputs remain incompletely reviewed. Combined-option GNU candidate d7d42ac4 passed startup, numerical, TLS, native byte capture, mapped-source and compiler-notice checks, plus 33 container and 29 HTTPS checks on separately owned runtime infrastructure. All 927 mapped native bodies remain available by verified hash after cleanup. All 107 bodies without byte-identical package candidates were regenerated exactly from the verified locked OpenSSL archive. All 927 mapped bodies have an Apache option in their captured file or selected generator notices; three explicit BSD alternatives and twenty distribution-conditional assembly generators remain qualified by the locked OpenSSL source origin. Additional public-domain origins, include inputs and unmapped content remain under review. It has no retained SipHash symbols or objects. Its external std contains non-allowlisted components that must not be bundled. Individual-file exceptions, unmapped or inlined content, external-runtime distribution and production adoption remain uncleared. See licensing.md and runtime-link-audit.md. Corrected GNU candidate d1275bc2 passed source/notice checks, 35 isolated container checks and 29 HTTPS checks. It preserves 1,872 files covering 1,873 native paths and 252 system paths; all 927 mapped native body hashes match the preceding candidate. Earlier inherited user-only compiler rules omitted system headers. Conservative selected-input coverage includes 248 system paths, whose macros, constants and unmapped content remain under review. Production packaging is unchanged and licensing is uncleared. The experimental character adapter candidate 94f7a1e4 passed the full byte/EOF fixture, source and notice checks, 35 container checks, 29 HTTPS checks and the original four-track album in both official clients. A fresh 1,034-command preprocessor replay and independent verification of 3,102 compressed artifacts no longer report __tobody in the joined use-or-test set. The socket declaration macro remains for review; absence of that character macro does not clear header contributions or whole-runtime licensing. The retained backend was restored to the static image with all 50 saved rows matching observed plays. See runtime-link-audit.md#external-c-character-conversion. External-TLS candidate 5f872697 passed preprocessing byte capture, named-object ownership, source/notice checks, 35 container and 29 HTTPS checks. Its external standard library must not be bundled; production adoption and complete binary licensing remain uncleared. See runtime-link-audit.md#preprocessing-only-inputs.

jellyfin_12_behavior.detail: 106 of 364 operation declarations match; this does not measure compatible behavior. Current core 66e7213d passed 35 container and 29 local HTTPS checks, including active FFmpeg shutdown, video resume and metadata/user-data persistence after restart. Both official web and Qt 6 Desktop completed the original four-track FLAC album with automatic advancement, fifteen successful playback responses each and exactly one added play per track without a reset. Web active audio and Desktop audio EOF were observed. The retained backend kept its identity, grants, mounts, saved user data, playlists, studio favorites and original media hashes through explicit container recreation. Audio metadata now registers bounded missing artist names with persistent library identities. Current permitted credit sources govern visibility; inactive identities and favorites survive rescans. The preceding tag-artist image matched twenty-two scoped membership comparisons, five artist details, four role lists and six mixed audio/album sort queries against the preserved public Jellyfin 12 reference. Five empty-credit queries and sixteen preceding artist-list queries also matched; two uncounted orders remain qualified. Earlier eighteen numeric-order queries, nine tagged audio cases, twenty-nine personal-filter observations and forty-six partial user-data cases retain their preceding scopes in acceptance.md. Both preceding official clients loaded Artists and Album artists and a generated artist's album page. The preceding web run also completed the generated album-artist card's two credited tracks, with seven successful playback responses and exactly one added play on each; no active-media DOM observation was captured during that shorter run. Comparisons exclude album display names, plain-track Album fallback, parent DTO fields, artwork, genres and global unscoped defaults. Four Items boolean query fields now accept observed case, whitespace and empty-optional forms. Fifty of 64 reference projections match status, ordered IDs/names/types, totals and offsets; five disabled-count and nine existing folder-filter observations remain qualified. All six original capitalized-recursion sort queries match. Unrequested SortName presence and other boolean binders remain open. See jellyfin12-catalog-booleans.md. Album naming/creation, album-only artist registration, ambiguous names, wider collation, embedded images, broader tag formats, virtual-item edits, broader rating filters, complete recommendations/collections and full Jellyfin 12 behavior remain incomplete. General Desktop video acceptance, native AAC, arbitrary seeking, audible quality, broader clients and scale remain unvalidated. Native final-position inconsistency remains unresolved; qualified negative-value and ended duplicate-stop differences are documented. See compatibility.md and jellyfin12-tagged-artists.md. Physical albums now expose visible direct audio ChildCount and summed RunTimeTicks. Nine detail/list projections for two original albums match the public reference values; artist-only counters are omitted. Database checks cover hidden and restricted tracks, missing durations, overflow and immediate grant revocation. Album counts persist across restart. Both official clients display the four-track count and rounded duration on the new image. Broader album behavior and the reference grant-revocation child-query difference remain qualified. See jellyfin12-album-counts.md. A preceding experimental external-TLS official web queue exposed a concurrent explicit-session progress/start race: initial progress returned 404 before start completed. That failed attempt and its saved plays remain recorded. The startup repair extends the existing bounded wait to explicit IDs without changing ownership, item or current-run constraints. A database-backed HTTP regression failed before the fix and passed afterward for an opaque ID and a UUID without ItemId in progress. The current official-client runs returned all fifteen playback reports successfully per client; their passing web trace did not reproduce concurrent request ordering. Joined evidence covers 262 source fingerprints and all 50 saved rows without a reset. See jellyfin12-playback-behavior.md#concurrent-start-and-progress.
